consensus_summary: Babel/Babylon symbolizes human pride, organized rebellion against God, an idolatrous world empire attempting to make a name for itself, and a counterfeit or anti-God system opposed to the city of God.
book_summary: A self-made kingdom that builds a name against heaven, acts as an empire ruling over others, and serves as a counterfeit to God's covenant.
consensus_core_identification: Archetypal symbol of human pride, self-exaltation, and an oppressive, idolatrous world empire opposed to God.
book_core_identification: A self-made kingdom building a name against heaven and an empire functioning as a covenant counterfeit.
rationale: The book's definition perfectly matches the consensus, employing the exact biblical imagery of a self-made kingdom trying to reach heaven (making a name for itself) and functioning as a counterfeit or opponent to God's covenant city.
strongest_objection: One might argue 'covenant counterfeit' introduces a specific covenantal theology not universally present in the consensus, but the consensus widely acknowledges the 'two cities' contrast and Babylon as the archetypal anti-God system, making this a difference in phrasing rather than substance.
